content: Health/status anti-patterns: (1) synchronous dependency checks on every probe - thundering herd during restarts, DoS surface; instead async background checks cached ~1s refresh so /health stays <10ms. (2) overchecking failed deps - circuit breaker + backoff, timeouts < probe interval, dedicated pools. (3) liveness that checks deps -> restart storms on DB blip (LinkedIn/ASP.NET incidents); separate endpoints. (4) degraded-but-serving returned as 503 removes instance for non-critical failure - warn-state 200 with alert; 503 only when truly can't serve. (5) collapse degraded into green 'mood ring' ok:true. (6) disjoint probe path (stub /health 200 while real path broken) - probe a cheap real op; for file-backed service probe the actual state-file freshness the app serves. (7) health endpoints calling other health endpoints (cascading graphs). (8) same-endpoint-for-liveness-and-readiness restart loops. (9) exposing dep internals/hostnames in public health body.
